name: Vagisil BV
headline: Vagisil BV — Learning Journey E01
subtitle: Iterative Experiment Platform · 2026.05.05
background: Vagisil is expanding its portfolio with a breakthrough solution for Bacterial Vaginosis (BV). Unlike traditional treatments that require multi-day applications, this new product is formulated to provide effective symptom relief in a single dose, with visible results within just one day.
objective: Establish a hierarchy of information for the packaging to ensure the most compelling benefits are communicated first.

methodology.format: Static banners (3 packaging claims), each driving to a dedicated landing page with add-to-cart
methodology.kpi: Stopping Power (unique link clicks / reach) and Closing Power (add to cart / landing page visits), plus Holding Power and Overall Score

narrative.body: Three banners (Banner 001, 002, 003), one per packaging claim: "Kills 99% of bacteria that causes BV", "95% of women said their symptoms were gone in 1 day" and "Relief in just 1 day". The annex includes the packaging shown in the creatives.

rounds.outcome: The claim "Relief in just 1 day" delivers the highest Stopping and Closing Power, making it the overall top-performing claim. While the remaining claims show similar levels of Stopping Power, "95% of women said their symptoms were gone in 1 day" achieves a slightly higher Closing Power than "Kills 99% of bacteria that causes BV", although the difference is not statistically significant.

learnings: "Relief in just 1 day" delivered the highest Stopping Power (3.51%, statistically better than both other claims) and the highest Closing Power (17.09%), making it the overall top-performing claim.
"95% of women said their symptoms were gone in 1 day" achieved a slightly higher Closing Power than "Kills 99% of bacteria that causes BV", but the difference is not statistically significant.
All age groups delivered Stopping Power above the upper limit of the IEP Benchmark (1.18%-2.48%), showing strong overall attention to the BV proposition.

Ages 36-45 and 46-55 responded most strongly: "Relief in just 1 day" was statistically superior in Stopping Power for 36-45 (4.86%, the best result across the test) and delivered the highest Closing Power of the test in 46-55 (20.83%).
Ages 18-25 showed the weakest conversion: Closing Power fell below the IEP Benchmark for two of the three claims, with "Relief in just 1 day" the highest directional result.
In 46-55, both "Relief in just 1 day" and "Kills 99% of bacteria that causes BV" were statistically higher than "95% of women..." in Stopping Power.
recommendations: Lead the packaging information hierarchy with "Relief in just 1 day", the top-performing claim in both Stopping and Closing Power.
Use "95% of women said their symptoms were gone in 1 day" as a supporting claim, given its directionally higher Closing Power versus "Kills 99% of bacteria that causes BV".
Consider age-specific emphasis: the speed-of-relief message resonates most with women 36-55, while the 18-25 segment converts below benchmark and may need a different approach.

name: Vagisil Wash
headline: Vagisil Wash — Project Compass E02R01
subtitle: Project Compass E02R01 · LIVE — results streaming directly from the Meta API while the experiment runs.
background: Itch Protect Mousse Wash was introduced to the Vagisil portfolio to replace the 12 oz Itch Protect gel wash to reverse sales softness and reinvigorate the product. Mousse wash is an increasingly popular format and adds to the premiumization of the brands. Since the launch in Spring 2026, this new format and design does not seem to be resonating with consumers and sales have been slow to ramp up. Hypotheses for poor performance are that "Itch Protect" is not an intuitive product benefit and consumers don't understand what problem the product solves. Mousse is also more expensive but is not delivering on perceived superiority to gel wash. The current packaging is doing a better job at communicating format rather than function (mousse vs. benefit to consumer). Communication and design feel more clinical than reassuring (comforting).
objective: Which concept has more Stopping Power at shelf and which concept drives more purchase intent (Closing Power): "Sensitive" or "Hydration+"? Benchmark "Sensitive" and "Hydration+" against Summer's Eve Simply Sensitive concept, and against the current "Itch Protect" Wash.
hypothesis: "Itch Protect" is not an intuitive product benefit and consumers don't understand what problem the product solves; the current packaging communicates format (mousse) rather than function, and the communication and design feel more clinical than reassuring.

methodology.format: Static banners (5 concepts/claims), each driving to a dedicated landing page with add-to-cart
methodology.field: In field since July 2026 (E02R01, deck dated 2026.07.27)
methodology.kpi: Stopping Power (unique link clicks / reach) and Closing Power (add to cart / landing page visits)

name: Anti-Itch Claims Testing
headline: Vagisil Max Strength Anti-Itch Creme — Project Compass E03R01
subtitle: Project Compass E03R01 · 2026.09.09 — approved by Combe; Phase 1 launching. Results will stream here as the campaign runs.
background:
Vagisil's Maximum Strength Anti-Itch Creme (20% benzocaine, 3% resorcinol) is the #1 anti-itch cream on the market and the cornerstone of the brand.

Over the last two years the anti-itch business shows a steady decline (L52W: -6.5% dollars, -5.5% units), driven by compressed shelf space (category TDPs down ~700 pts), competition from niche and value brands, and consumers shifting from problem-solution toward prevention.

The company's position is clear: the medicated positioning is not negotiable. The goal is to return this $20-30M business to growth.
objective:
Determine which claims have the most Stopping Power for the hero product across nine claim territories: medicated efficacy, speed, duration, root-cause control, microbiome/pH, skin barrier, sensory, free-from and trust.

The test follows a control design: the base claim (“Strongest medicine for intense itch”) runs alone as the control, four alternative anchors run alone, and every other banner adds a single attribute on top of the base claim, so any change in Stopping Power is attributable to that attribute.

Top performers advance to Phase 2: six claims, full journey, Stopping & Closing Power.
hypothesis:
Key strategic questions:
· Does the current product deliver on consumer expectations?
· Should the brand keep leaning into problem-solution messaging, or can prevention claims (pH, microbiome, skin barrier) add attention on top of the medicated message?
· What are the largest barriers to purchase?

Stretch claims not supportable by the current formula (pH balanced, restores the microbiome) are tested intentionally as input for future formula work, and three ingredient claims (ceramides, hyaluronic acid, gooseberry) run as innovation input.

methodology.format: 24 static banners in 3 formats (16:9, 9:16 and 3:4, Meta-safe zones respected): 1 control claim, 4 alternative anchors tested alone, and 19 base-plus-single-attribute variants. All five free-from claims included, woven into base-plus-attribute banners.
methodology.field: Phase 1 traffic campaign — September 2026 (E03R01, compass dated 2026.09.09). Results expected within ~3 weeks of launch.
methodology.kpi: Stopping Power (unique link clicks / reach); Phase 2 adds Closing Power (add to cart / landing page visits)
